_doc: Stream C (play-test 5, T25 ANGLING) — the NUMBERS of the angling loop, read by js/rules/fishing.js. No fish, junk, legends, recipes or rods live here: those are stream E's data/provinces/angling.json and are handed to createFishing(numbers, content). `wait`: seconds from the bobber landing to the bite (always clamped to min..max; bait/rod `wait` are fractions added to 1, a pool multiplies by poolMult). `bite`: the window to press, ms, growing a little with skill. `kinds`: the share of casts that are a monster / crate / junk / legend — the rest are fish; junk falls from junk.at0 to junk.at100 with skill and is multiplied by junk.poolMult in a pool; crate is used only when E's file has no crates.chance. `rarity`: weights by source (open water, pool tier 1/2/3); `skillShift` multiplies a rarity's weight by 1 + skill/divisor. `pools`: skill gate, catches before it is fished out, how much sooner it bites. `tug`: per rarity — ms long, band (share of the bar that is safe), need (share of the time the marker must stay in it), pull (how hard the fish drags), speed, jitter; skill widens the band by up to bandPerSkill at 100 and a rod's bonus.band multiplies it, capped at bandMax. `heft`: size in cm from which a catch is heavy / huge. `size`: frac = u^k with k from at0 to at100 (lower k = bigger fish); price = base x (priceMin + priceSpan x frac). `xp`: per catch by rarity, + perFishSkill x the fish's own skill requirement, first of a species adds firstMult x base, a personal best adds `best`. `level`: xp to go from level L to L+1 = a + b L + c L^2, levels 1..max.

xp._mult: round 11 (stream P, live #10): every catch's experience is multiplied by `mult` (3) — the profession pace was tripled for gathering and making alike

value._doc: owner feedback 7 (V2): a catch's gold = the species' own price (E's angling.json: its worth relative to other fish) x the size curve x rarity x mult x (1 + perBand x (zone level - 1)). Common fish are worth little, the prized few a lot, and the same water pays more in a higher zone. TUNED by stream E (economy lead, tools/sim-economy.mjs): mult 1.22, perBand 0.005 (it was 1 and 0.1), rarity factors nearly flat (0.9 / 1 / 1.1 / 1.2; they were 0.6 / 0.9 / 1.6 / 2.5). The spread between rarities is in E's species prices (angling.json: common 1-3, uncommon 10-20, rare 28-40, epic 80-180) and higher zones already hold the better species, so a second rarity factor and a steep zone factor on top made tier-3 pools pay three times questing.
